<%*
/* Weekly Summary Template — the skeleton for Courses/Weekly.md.
 *
 * Courses/Weekly.md is a single rolling note, regenerated by the
 * /courses:summary slash command and overwritten each run. Its history lives
 * in git, not in a folder of dated files.
 *
 * The window matches the command's: today through Sunday 23:59 of the current
 * Mon-Sun week. Running it on a Wednesday covers Wed-Sun. Only day headings
 * inside the window are emitted, so the skeleton never asks you to fill in a
 * day that has already gone.
 *
 * This produces the empty structure. The command fills it. If you are creating
 * the note by hand, everything below the frontmatter is yours to overwrite.
 */

const start = moment().startOf("day");
const end = moment().endOf("isoWeek").startOf("day");   /* Sunday */
const monday = moment().startOf("isoWeek");

const days = [];
for (let d = start.clone(); d.isSameOrBefore(end, "day"); d.add(1, "day")) {
  days.push(d.clone());
}

/* Course codes in the H3s are what makes this note searchable a month later:
 * `CS4530` finds every week you had work for it. */
const section = d => `## ${d.format("dddd")} — ${d.format("MMM D")}

### 

- [ ] 
`;

tR = `---
tags:
  - weekly
  - courses
  - northeastern
type: weekly
week_start: ${monday.format("YYYY-MM-DD")}
week_end: ${end.format("YYYY-MM-DD")}
generated: ${moment().format("YYYY-MM-DD")}
status: raw
---
# Week of ${monday.format("ddd MMM D")} — ${end.format("ddd MMM D, YYYY")}

> [!abstract] Window
> ${start.format("ddd YYYY-MM-DD")} → ${end.format("ddd YYYY-MM-DD")} 23:59 ET
> Regenerate with \`/courses:summary\`. This note is overwritten on each run —
> history is in git.

## Do First

1. 
2. 
3. 

${days.map(section).join("\n")}
## Overdue

## No Due Date

## Flags

## Related

- [[Courses]]
- [[Fall 2026 Calendar]]
`;
%>
